summary: First post-relaunch batch (cycle ~1224, lane tdd-structural-test-reachability-probe): minted phase flake-rerun-scan failed its contract [bad_verdict: no parseable verdict] on agy-tmux (blocks 1-2), CLI ESCALATION fired correctly at block 2 (agy-tmux -> claude-tmux, first live firing), and the ESCALATED CLI FAILED THE SAME WAY — block 3, circuit open, gate demoted enforce->advisory for the rest of the run. Two independent model families producing the identical no-parseable-verdict violation kills the model-property hypothesis for this instance (batch-18/21 evidence had claude COMPLYING where agy failed). The probable defect classes, in check order: (1) the minted phase's prompt/contract template never instructs the verdict line or names a different artifact than the phase writes (compare intent-delta-contract-path-skew — the contract gate verifying a file the phase was never asked to write); (2) the mint pipeline (advisor phase mint) generates contracts with RequireVerdict but a deliverable spec lacking the verdict section; (3) verdict parsed from the wrong artifact in minted-phase dispatch. NOTE the system otherwise behaved exactly as designed: escalation fired, breaker opened as last resort, demotion WARN carried all four facts (phase/cli/escalation-ran/violation), and the CYCLE STILL PASSED on its floor gates (ADR-0072 demote-don't-brick). The cost is that every future mint of a verdict-less contract demotes that run's gate — later phases ship ungated — so this recurs until the TEMPLATE side is fixed.
